options: A Salesforce-specific scripting language
An XML-based standard for exchanging authentication and authorization data between an IdP and SP
A type of permission set
A REST API for querying Salesforce records
questions.explain: SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) is an open, XML-based standard for exchanging authentication and authorization data between identity and service providers.

questions.q: What part of a SAML assertion prevents it from being replayed after it should have expired?
options: The AttributeStatement
The Conditions element's NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter validity window
The Subject element
The digital signature alone
questions.explain: The Conditions element defines a validity window; an assertion presented outside that window is rejected, which limits the damage a captured/replayed assertion could do.

questions.q: In the SAML Web Browser SSO POST flow, what does the browser do after the IdP builds a signed assertion?
options: It stores the assertion in a cookie permanently
It auto-submits an HTML form that POSTs the assertion to the SP's Assertion Consumer Service URL
It emails the assertion to the SP's administrator
It converts the assertion into an OAuth token before sending it
questions.explain: The IdP returns the signed assertion inside an auto-submitting form, which the browser POSTs to the SP's ACS URL, where it's validated.

questions.q: What tool does Salesforce provide specifically to decode and troubleshoot a captured SAML assertion?
options: The Setup Audit Trail
The SAML Assertion Validator
The Permission Set Analyzer
Health Check
questions.explain: The SAML Assertion Validator, available on the Single Sign-On Settings page, decodes a captured assertion and checks it against the org's SAML configuration.

questions.q: Why must the Issuer field on Salesforce's SAML Single Sign-On Setting exactly match the identity provider's configuration?
options: It doesn't need to match; Salesforce ignores the Issuer field
Because it's purely cosmetic and only shown in the Setup UI
Because Salesforce checks the Issuer against every incoming assertion, and rejects assertions whose issuer doesn't match
Because it determines the user's profile
questions.explain: The Issuer value must match the Entity ID the IdP places in its assertions. A mismatch causes Salesforce to reject otherwise-valid assertions, a very common real-world SSO failure cause.
